items.title: P.A.L.I
items.decryption: Use PALI to categorize Gupta sources: Puranas/Epics were rewritten, Accounts (Fa-Hien/I-tsing), Literature (Sanskrit classics), and Inscriptions (Allahabad Pillar).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing the Allahabad Pillar (Samudragupta) with the Iron Pillar at Mehrauli (Chandragupta II/Chandra).
Assuming 'Golden Age' implies prosperity for all castes; sources actually indicate the rise of the Shudra status to some extent.
Ignoring that Fa-Hien never mentions the name 'Gupta' or 'Chandragupta' in his travelogue.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Literary

  • Kalidasa's works: Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta.
  • Vishakhadatta: Mudrarakshasa, Devichandraguptam.
  • Puranas: Final compilation phase.

Numismatic

  • Gold coins: Called 'Dinaras'.
  • Represented kings in various avatars (Veena player, Lion slayer).
  • Reflect economic prosperity and trade.
  • Mindmap of Evidence:
    • Inscriptions:
      • Prayag Prashasti (Harisena): Detailed list of Samudragupta's conquests.
      • Mehrauli Iron Pillar: Mentions Chandra's victory over Vanga and Balkh.
    • Foreign Accounts:
      • Fa-Hien (Fo-Kuo-Ki): Describes the administration, religious tolerance, and condition of Magadha.
